title: U.S. House · Nevada's 1st District
area: Central Las Vegas and Clark County, including Henderson-area neighborhoods, in southern Nevada.

context.text: Incumbent Dina Titus (D) faced a primary challenge and advanced from the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary. Carrie Buck (R), a Nevada state senator, advanced from the Republican primary. The National Republican Congressional Committee named Buck to its "MAGA Majority" support program for candidates in Democratic-held districts; the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee named Titus to its "Frontline" program for vulnerable incumbents. Steven St John and Bobby Khan, both with no political party affiliation, also qualified for the general-election ballot.

summary.text: Dina Titus is the Democratic incumbent for Nevada's 1st Congressional District, which she has represented since 2013 after one earlier term in the House (2009-2011). A political scientist, she taught at UNLV for decades and served in the Nevada Senate, including as minority leader, before entering Congress. She is campaigning on affordability.

background.text: Born in Thomasville, Georgia, and grew up in Tifton, Georgia, according to Ballotpedia; her official biography says she grew up in Tifton with her parents and a younger sister.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the College of William and Mary, a master's degree from the University of Georgia, and a doctorate from Florida State University.

Taught American and Nevada government and political science classes at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, from 1979 until her retirement in 2011; her official biography describes her as a non-fiction writer known for expertise on the history and policy of nuclear power, weaponry and waste.
Served in the Nevada Senate representing District 7 for 20 years until 2008, including as Senate Minority Leader from 1993 to 2009 according to her official biography.

Won election to the U.S. House from Nevada's 3rd District in 2008 and lost re-election in 2010 to Joe Heck by less than one percentage point; she then won the 1st District seat in 2012 and has been re-elected since, including in 2024.

Sits on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, where her official biography says she is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee (2025-2026).

Her official biography describes her as dean of Nevada's congressional delegation, vice chair of the Hellenic Caucus, a founding member of the Colorado River Caucus, and a longtime opponent of nuclear waste storage at Yucca Mountain; it says she introduced legislation to ban bump stocks after the Las Vegas shooting and played a role in the Brightline West high-speed rail project.
According to her official biography, she has been married to UNLV professor Thomas C. Wright for more than 40 years.

summary.text: Carrie Buck is the Republican nominee for Nevada's 1st Congressional District and a sitting Nevada state senator from Henderson. A longtime educator, she taught in North Las Vegas, was principal of a Henderson elementary school, and led the Pinecrest Academy charter schools before winning her Senate seat in 2020. Her campaign website says she is running on parents' rights, border security, funding police and ending taxes on tips, and the National Republican Congressional Committee has named her to its program for candidates in Democratic-held districts.

background.text: Born in Sioux City, Iowa, where she grew up; the Nevada Independent reports her father was an accountant and her mother worked for the telephone company. Her campaign website says she was raised on a small farm.
Earned a bachelor's degree in elementary education from Montana State University (1995), a master's degree from the University of Phoenix (1998), and a Ph.D. from Nova Southeastern University (2006).

Moved to Las Vegas in 1996 after college; her campaign website says she began her career teaching fifth grade in North Las Vegas. She also worked as an English-language-learner specialist and instructional coach with the Clark County School District.
Became principal of C.T. Sewell Elementary School in Henderson in 2006 and served there about eight years; she received a Milken Educator Award in 2008.

Was recruited to Pinecrest Academy of Nevada around 2014, where she was principal and executive director; became president of the Pinecrest Foundation, a nonprofit supporting charter school scholarships, in 2019.

Lost a 2016 race for Nevada State Senate District 5 to Democrat Joyce Woodhouse by fewer than 500 votes; won the open seat in 2020 after Woodhouse was termed out, and was re-elected in 2024 over Democrat Jennifer Atlas.
Committee assignments in the 2025-2026 Nevada Senate: Education; Finance; and Growth and Infrastructure.

Launched her campaign for Nevada's 1st District while serving in the state Senate; the Nevada Independent reports she has President Donald Trump's endorsement. She won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary.

Her campaign website says she and her husband Eric, a retired Deputy Chief of Police, have four sons and are local small business owners; in a 2024 Ballotpedia survey she described herself as the wife of a Henderson police captain and mother of four sons, two of whom serve in the U.S. Armed Forces.

priorities.text: Education: expanding Opportunity Scholarships, requiring state receivership of the lowest-performing schools, and giving parents more say in their children's schooling.
Public safety: sponsored legislation to tighten restrictions and strengthen penalties for human traffickers and fentanyl traffickers, and works with a coalition on preventing child trafficking.
Economy and housing: says she has sponsored legislation reforming cosmetology licensing and the state employment/training department, and is focused on the rising cost of living and housing.

positions.summary: Says she believes firmly in expanded funding of Opportunity Scholarships, which fund private-school tuition for lower-income families, and that parents alone should make critical decisions about their child's education.
positions.quote: I believe firmly in exanded funding of Opportunity Scholarships which would allow more underprivileged families to send their children to schools that are the best fit for them.

positions.summary: Voted for a 2023 law shielding out-of-state abortion patients and Nevada providers from prosecution under other states' abortion bans, but voted against a state constitutional amendment establishing a right to reproductive freedom, including abortion.

record.text: Voted yes on Assembly Bill No. 383 (establishing a right to reproductive health care services, excluding abortion, and requiring Medicaid coverage of certain contraception), which passed the Nevada Senate 16-5 on June 5, 2023.

Voted yes on Senate Bill No. 131 (shielding abortion patients from out of state and Nevada abortion providers from investigation or prosecution under another state's abortion laws), which passed the Nevada Senate 15-6 on April 19, 2023.

Voted no on Senate Joint Resolution No. 7 (proposing a state constitutional amendment establishing a right to reproductive freedom, including abortion), which passed the Nevada Senate 13-8 on April 17, 2023.

summary.text: Steven St John is a no-party candidate for Nevada's 1st Congressional District. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he describes himself as a hospital chaplain in Las Vegas for nearly a decade and says he is running on healthcare, housing and cost-of-living issues and on working across party lines.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from New Trier High School and a master's degree from San Diego State University (1976, per Ballotpedia's education listing).

Ballotpedia reports he previously worked in advertising, marketing and business development, and as a chaplain; in his 2026 survey he describes about a decade as a hospital chaplain in Las Vegas and says he served as a chaplain under Mayor Goodman's faith initiative, ministering to people experiencing homelessness.
In his survey he says he was self-employed as a young man doing fence refinishing and home improvement work, and that he experienced homelessness for several months in the early 1980s.
Ballotpedia states that he and his wife live in Henderson, Nevada. In his survey he says he is not a career politician.

summary.text: Bobby Khan is a no-party candidate for Nevada's 1st Congressional District. Born in Scotland, he is a former luxury car dealer who, according to Casino.org, pleaded guilty to a federal wire fraud charge and served time in federal prison; he says he is running on justice-system reform, veterans' benefits and ending federal taxes on gambling winnings.

background.text: Born in Edinburgh, Scotland, according to Ballotpedia; Casino.org reports he was born Babar Khan in Scotland. He graduated from Absegami High School and attended Philadelphia University.

In his Ballotpedia survey he describes himself as the son of immigrants who began working in his father's restaurant at age 12, then left college for the car business, ran luxury dealerships in his 20s and started his own exotic car company.

Casino.org reports he owned Emporio Motor Group, a New Jersey luxury car dealership, was indicted on wire fraud charges in 2014, was a federal fugitive for six years, surrendered in 2020, and pleaded guilty to a charge involving $550,000 in losses, after which he served time in federal prison. According to Casino.org, he has characterized the conviction as the result of prosecutorial overreach.
